purpose: Pinned source identities and acquisition points for every native component this repository may build, vendor or redistribute. This file records identity and licence *evidence*. It is not itself a legal clearance: per-component clearance decisions live in components.json.

pinKinds.releasePin: Identity fixed to a named upstream revision or published asset digest. Re-verifiable by anyone from the cited URL.
pinKinds.referencePin: Identity fixed to a documented upstream reference (a URL, a version string, a commit) where the artefact itself is not present here and no digest has been computed.
pinKinds.observation: A hash or state measured on this machine from a file that was NOT produced by this repository's build. Descriptive research evidence only. Never a release pin, never a substitute for a reproduction.

conventions.observationRule: Any entry with pinKind=observation lives under an `observations` key and MUST NOT be referenced as a pin by a build, a bundle manifest or a download. observations.observedBinaries is the canonical four-entry record (stock core, fork core, aji.dll, aji_trt.dll) and is transcribed from plan.md section 3.2; the per-directory detail elsewhere in the same block is supporting context, not a second set of pins.

fileIntegrity.digestInventory: The source carries a per-file SHA-256 inventory on this record ('sourceDigestsMeasuredLocally', 'models', 'files' or 'releaseAssets'). mikai_manifest_check recomputes every listed digest against the matching --source-root and fails on any mismatch. This is the only mode that makes a source's bytes checkable today.
fileIntegrity.commitIdentity: The source is pinned by revision, not by per-file digest: its artefact is either not present locally or is a whole archive too large to inventory file by file. Identity is the commit SHA, the git tree SHA and, where available, an archive digest. mikai_manifest_check requires the revision fields to be present and well-formed; it does not claim byte-level integrity it cannot compute.
fileIntegrity.documentationOnly: A build-time toolchain or an out-of-scope research input. Identity is a version string. Nothing is shipped and nothing is redistributed, so no digest is required. 'not adopted' items and non-redistributable toolchains land here.

digestPolicy.shape: Every digest this repository records is lowercase hex SHA-256 and is written as exactly 64 characters. mikai_manifest_check rejects any other form, so a truncated or upper-cased digest fails instead of silently mismatching later.
digestPolicy.twoIndependentComputations: A digest recorded as a pin is computed twice - once from the artefact in hand, once from the same artefact at the cited upstream revision - and both must agree. A single local measurement is recorded only under observations, never as a pin.
digestPolicy.missingMeansNull: A digest that was not computed is written as null, never as a placeholder string and never omitted. null means 'not computed', and it is never read as 'no digest required' by a build.
digestPolicy.observationDigestsAreNeverVerified: Observation digests are recorded but deliberately NOT recomputed by mikai_manifest_check. They describe files this repository did not build; re-hashing them would imply an integrity claim that does not hold. They are format-checked only.

sources.deliberateOmission: No cuDNN and no cuBLAS. The RIFE and spatial engine build passes --tacticSources=-CUDNN,-CUBLAS,-CUBLAS_LT, and the pinned kernels use only cudaMalloc/cudaMemcpy plus the driver API. Shipping either would add hundreds of megabytes for no reachable code path. This omission is recorded so a later reader does not read the absence as an oversight.
sources.deliberateOmissionCaveat: Suppressing those tactic sources changes which TensorRT tactics are available, which changes the numbers in a generated engine and therefore the engine's digest. Engine digests are consequently NOT portable across a change to this list; an engine built with cudnn tactics enabled is not interchangeable with one built without them. See components.json#runtime.cuda-cudart.

The reference package's notice calling the file DirectML_LICENSE.txt is a naming inconsistency on that side, not a different licence.

sources.role: RIFE interpolation weights for M12: v4.14 full/lite, each with and without ensemble
sources.fileIntegrityReason: The four graphs are pinned by their acquired archive SHA-256 (3fcf3429f3bb661d15c59aa58ed7ba28c0ca7f79e2388f8e0165dd8bbe0648f9), which was published in the GitHub release note and reproduced exactly on extraction. Individual per-graph digests are not recorded here; they are computed and compared at acquisition time and recorded in native/rife-acquisition.md.

requiredFileNames.derivation: rife_model_name() in src/aji_trt.cpp:934-946 and src/aji_dml.cpp:1311-1323: code '414' -> "rife_v4.14"; a four-digit code ending in '1' -> "rife_v4.14_lite"; ensemble appends "_ensemble". The consumer appends ".onnx". The two suffix branches are independent axes (_lite keys on the code, _ensemble on a separate boolean) and compose, so all four combinations below are reached and required.
requiredFileNames.crossReference: the same enumeration exists upstream in AmusementClub/vs-mlrt scripts/vsmlrt.py (RIFEModel v4_14=414, v4_14_lite=4141; version string v{major}.{minor}{lite|heavy}{_ensemble}); files land under models/rife/rife_<version>.onnx (implementation 1) or models/rife_v2/ (implementation 2)

provenanceChain.note: "The content of these links is under the same MIT license as this project. 'lite' means using similar training framework, but lower computational cost model."  The author README and LICENSE are read at the pinned commit above.

licence.scopeLimit: The MIT text grants rights in "this software and associated documentation files". The author's README sentence - "The content of these links is under the same MIT license as this project" - is an affirmative, specific grant by the copyright holder that the linked model weights are MIT, and is accepted here as licence evidence for the weights themselves. No per-file licence text accompanies the weights, so the grant is a project-level statement rather than an embedded notice. Both v4.14 and v4.14.lite checkpoints were acquired into original-checkpoints/ and compared tensor-by-tensor against the four graphs; every stored weight matched (native/rife-acquisition.md §5.1). No ensemble weight artefact is published in Practical-RIFE's links: each ensemble graph's initializer set is byte-identical to its base graph's.

provenanceChain.note: The paper project. Provides HD model archives on Google Drive/Baidu; no ensemble artefact and no per-version permissibility statement.

provenanceChain.layer: ONNX export used as the conversion input
provenanceChain.note: the shim's conversion tool converts "the vsmlrt RIFE v1 (video_player) ONNX models"; vsmlrt resolves them from models/rife/rife_<version>.onnx

acquisition.digestGap: GitHub reports digest: null for both assets, so no sha256 is pinned upstream. Any copy taken must be hashed locally and the hash recorded here before use.

licence.scopeNote: This licence covers vs-mlrt's own code. No vs-mlrt code is shipped here; only the ONNX *output* of its export is consumed. Whether the GPL-3.0 code licence extends to the exported model files is a legal question that is not settled by the licence text alone and is not asserted either way here.

provenanceChain.layer: the exact fp16 graphs the shim consumes
provenanceChain.releaseNote: "vsmlrt v1 (video_player) RIFE models converted to fp16 with the GridSample sampling-grid math kept in an fp32 island (tools/convert_rife_fp16.py)." 47 models (rife 4.7-4.26 incl. lite/heavy/ensemble variants), 1011 MB -> 507 MB on disk. The package manifest's deps.rife = "models-rife-fp16-1".

provenanceLinkage.declared: The release note states the conversion input was the vsmlrt v1 (video_player) RIFE models, and the shim's own conversion tool states it converts exactly those. That is a documented chain naming vsmlrt as the immediate input.
provenanceLinkage.weightDataClosed: CLOSED by direct comparison, with no execution. The author's own v4.14 / v4.14.lite checkpoints were acquired into original-checkpoints/ and compared tensor-by-tensor against ModelProto.graph.initializer of all four graphs: 128/128 names and shapes matched with FP32->FP16 round-to-nearest-even bytes identical across four comparisons (base->rife_v4.14 and base->rife_v4.14_ensemble, lite->rife_v4.14_lite and lite->rife_v4.14_lite_ensemble; base and ensemble initializer sets identical). The stored weight bytes are therefore the author's MIT v4.14 / v4.14.lite weights.
provenanceLinkage.stillOpen: Exporter identity and the non-weight graph material. The comparison reads initializers only, so it proves nothing about which exporter produced the graph structure - the fp16 GridSample fp32 island, the Transpose-built grids, the cast placement, the ensemble merge math or the fp16 conversion path. No upstream statement names the exporter of these specific files, the publishing repository declares no licence of its own, and the release assets carry no per-file notice. This is a provenance/rights gap for the file as an artefact, not a weight-data gap.
provenanceLinkage.machineReadable: original-checkpoints/weight-comparison.json (schemaVersion 1), produced by original-checkpoints/compare-weights.mjs (exit 0; it records licenseReady: false by design, because it compares stored weight bytes only)

licence.finding: The publishing repository declares no licence for its own source. That absence governs the repository's code and does not by itself determine the rights in the converted weight files it publishes - a converted graph does not automatically inherit the publisher's code status. The weight data now traces to the author's MIT checkpoints (see provenanceLinkage.weightDataClosed), but the files as artefacts additionally carry exporter-produced material with no per-file notice, so the rights basis for redistributing the graph files is not established.
licence.notAsserted: No permission and no prohibition on redistribution is asserted here. Weight-data provenance is established; whole-artefact redistribution rights are recorded as open.

localAvailability.ownedAcquisition: All four graphs are present and digest-verified under F:/ZKS/mikai-native-assets/rife/onnx/ - the owned acquisition, outside the repository and outside every tracked source tree, so nothing can be committed or accidentally vendored. native/rife-acquisition.md records the archive pin, extraction, structural check and the tensor-by-tensor weight comparison; native/videojanai-acquisition.md records the byte-identical comparison against component-rife.7z. No other local copy is referenced.
localAvailability.notClaimed: Acquisition and weight-data provenance are not a readiness claim: nothing was executed, built into an engine, bundled or exposed as Ready.

rebuildRecipe.purpose: re-link the DLLs that import the GNU runtime into DLLs with the compiler and winpthread runtime embedded, so the native closure needs no libstdc++-6 / libgcc_s_seh-1 / libwinpthread-1 and cannot collide with the Qt cohort
rebuildRecipe.exportReproduction: the exact export list of the shipped prefix DLL is read with objdump -p and written to a .def, so the linker pulls only the objects the original exported
rebuildRecipe.verifiedOutcome: measured 2026-10-04: all 13 rebuilt DLLs export exactly the same name sets as the prefix originals (cairo 415, cairo-gobject 35, fontconfig 246, freetype 220, gdk_pixbuf 136, graphite2 70, harfbuzz 1415, hwy 35, pango 514, pangocairo 35, pangoft2 96, pangowin32 35, rsvg 55 - zero missing, zero extra), and none of the 13 imports any of the three GNU runtime DLLs while the prefix copies of cairo, graphite2, harfbuzz and hwy do.
rebuildRecipe.honestLimit: an identical export set plus a byte-verified DLL is not a behavioural proof. The rebuild uses --allow-multiple-definition and statically links a private winpthread, which is a documented risk of silent symbol interposition rather than of a build failure; the consequence is that these 13 DLLs must still be exercised at run time before any claim about identical rendering behaviour is made. No run-time equivalence test is recorded here.

headerPair.role: the authoritative ABI definition; the shim is built from it
the consumer's mirror of the ABI; AJI_API_VERSION is at line 42

abi.headerPairFinding: Both headers declare AJI_API_VERSION 8, but they are NOT byte-identical and do NOT declare the same symbol set. The inference header declares 17 functions; the fork's mirror declares 16. The single difference is aji_rife_before_upscale, which the fork's header does not declare at all. The two files also differ in comment text (the fork's AJI_FMT_RGB10A2 comment omits the 'output is 4:2:0' clause, and it lacks the aji_infer output-format paragraph). Measured 2026-10-03: the two files differ at lines 53-56, 151 and 180-196. This is benign but must be recorded rather than assumed away - see exports[].declaredIn.
abi.invariant: the two headers must agree; an ABI change requires updating both, rebuilding both, and bumping the engine and mpv versions together

int aji_infer(aji_ctx *c, const aji_frame *in, const aji_frame *out, void *cu_stream)
int aji_infer_rife(aji_ctx *c, const aji_frame *a, const aji_frame *b, double t, const aji_frame *out, void *cu_stream)

exports.note: resolved and non-null-checked by the same gate, but not listed in the filter's explicit !p->api.* null condition; it is a direct-mode-only query

exports.resolution: resolved by name at vf_animejanai.c:1915-1916 and accepted as NULL. The fork's own aji.h mirror does NOT declare this function, which is why declaredIn is inferenceOnly.
resolved by name at vf_animejanai.c:1919 and accepted as NULL

exports.signature: int aji_resize(aji_ctx *c, const aji_frame *in, const aji_frame *out, void *cu_stream)
exports.resolution: resolved by name at vf_animejanai.c:1920 and accepted as NULL

abi.exportCountBasis: 17 is the authoritative ABI surface: the inference header declares exactly these 17 functions, and they are exactly the 17 names the fork's filter asks the shim for by name at vf_animejanai.c:1904-1925. The filter performs 17 dlsym lookups; 14 are in the non-null load gate, 3 are optional and may be NULL.
abi.resolutionMechanism: The filter never links the shim. It opens the DLL and resolves every symbol by name with dlsym (vf_animejanai.c:113 defines the lookup helper; 1904-1925 performs the lookups), then refuses to open at all if any of the 14 gated names is NULL, logging 'missing aji_* symbols (ABI version mismatch?)'. Optional names may be NULL and the filter degrades to a documented default: without aji_rife_before_upscale it runs upscale-then-RIFE; without aji_pre_resize and aji_resize it runs RIFE at source resolution.
abi.optionalNote: The three ordering/resize calls were added without an AJI_API_VERSION bump, which is exactly why the filter treats them as nullable: a caller built against an older header never queries them. Consequence for this manifest: the version macro alone does NOT describe the ABI surface, because the surface changed while the number stayed at 8. exports[] is the authoritative list; the macro is a compatibility label, not a contract.
abi.mismatchRule: Adding a symbol requires updating both headers, vf_animejanai.c and this list together, and does not require a version bump. REMOVING or changing the meaning of a symbol REQUIRES bumping AJI_API_VERSION, because a removed name cannot be distinguished from a load-time mismatch by the null gate alone - it would simply resolve to NULL and be treated as an optional degradation.
abi.engineVersionCoupling: The TensorRT engine cache is keyed on model identity, not on ABI version. A change to aji_frame's layout or to the meaning of a status code therefore invalidates cached engines as well as callers, and an engine built against the old meaning must be regenerated. Bumping AJI_API_VERSION without invalidating the cache produces a silent wrong-result failure rather than a load failure.

AJI_NVINFER.resolvesTo: the import library nvinfer_11.lib in AJI_TRT_ROOT, and at run time the nvinfer_11.dll that must sit beside the shipped aji_trt.dll
AJI_NVINFER.wrongValueFailureMode: leaving the default in place makes aji_trt fail to LINK with an unresolved nvinfer_10 symbol. That is a link-time failure rather than a silent runtime one, so it cannot yield a subtly wrong binary - but it also cannot be detected by inspecting a built DLL, so the pin must be carried on the build command line and never left to the default.
AJI_NVINFER.rule: TensorRT 11 is the target and TensorRT 10 is not a dependency. The default must be overridden explicitly; relying on it produces a link error for a library that is not present.

CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES.coverage: Turing (75), Ampere (80 and 86), Ada (89), Hopper (90), Blackwell consumer (100) and Blackwell datacenter (120), plus PTX for compute_120 so a future architecture JIT-compiles instead of dying with 'no kernel image is available for execution on the device'.
CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES.builderResourceCoupling: The seven real architectures correspond one-to-one with the TensorRT per-SM builder resource DLLs nvinfer_builder_resource_sm{75,80,86,89,90,100,120}_11.dll plus the ptx resource. This list and components.json#runtime.tensorrt-resources MUST stay in step: a kernel arch with no matching builder resource, or a resource with no matching kernel arch, is a closure defect that surfaces only at engine-build time on the affected GPU.
CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES.binariesAffected: aji_trt.dll only. aji.dll contains no device code and aji_dml.dll is a D3D11/D3D12 backend that never invokes nvcc, so neither is affected by this list.
CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES.rationale: kernel images for every supported generation Turing..Blackwell plus PTX so future architectures JIT-compile. Building only for the build machine's GPU produces a binary that dies on every other architecture.
CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES.trap: The CMakeLists fallback is guarded by if(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES) and CMake pre-defines the variable during project(), so the fallback never fires. Omitting the flag yields a single default arch. The list must always be passed explicitly.

cudaMinorDerivation.rule: never infer the CUDA minor from the TensorRT version
cudaMinorDerivation.reason: The CUDA flavour is encoded in NVIDIA's own artefact filename and is not derivable from the TensorRT version. NVIDIA's observed pairings wander - 11.0 pairs with 13.2, 11.1 with 13.3, 11.2 with 13.3, 11.3 with 13.4 - so any rule of the form 'TensorRT 11 implies CUDA 13.x' is a guess that has been wrong before and would be wrong again.
cudaMinorDerivation.evidence: the acquisition record for TensorRT-Enterprise-11.3.0.99-Windows-amd64-cuda-13.4-Release-external.zip, and animejanai-inference .github/workflows/build-linux.yml which pins TRT_VERSION 11.3.0.99 alongside TRT_CUDA '13.4'

engineBuild.tacticSuppressionEffect: changes which tactics the builder may select, so it changes the numerics inside a generated engine and therefore the engine's digest. engineBuild.noTrtexec: engines are built in-process through the TensorRT builder API, so trtexec.exe is a build-time convenience and is never a run-time dependency. That is what resolves ESC-5 by architecture rather than by permission.
